title: Late-time distance consistency and model-independent curvature inference with strong lensing, quasars, and galaxy clusters
comment: 18 pages, 6 figures, Accepted for publication in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (RAA)
summary: We revisit a late-time, model-independent distance-consistency framework that combines strong gravitational lensing systems (SGLS), ultraviolet/X-ray quasars (QSOs), and 38 Sunyaev--Zel'dovich/X-ray galaxy-cluster angular-diameter distances. The analysis focuses on systematics rather than on presenting a competitive curvature measurement. Starting from the 158-system SGLS catalog, we exclude 30 systems that violate the lensing-geometric requirement $D_{A,ls}/D_{A,s}<1$ in the isothermal reference case $γ_{\rm lens}=2$, leaving a fixed 128-system SGLS parent sample for cross-matching with 1598 QSOs. A deterministic maximum-cardinality, minimum-mismatch one-to-one assignment yields 100 SGLS--QSO pairs at the nominal $Δd/d=5\%$ threshold. We propagate the measured X-ray flux uncertainties and the intrinsic QSO scatter, and, crucially, we include the full $38\times38$ covariance induced by using the same QSO distances in the kernel-smoothed cluster predictions. With $Ω_K\sim\mathcal{U}[-10,10]$, the joint posterior is $Ω_K=2.085^{+1.634}_{-1.103}$ (68\%; central 95\% interval $[0.269,6.028]$). We do not interpret the positive shift as evidence for an open Universe. \added{This positive posterior offset is driven by cross-probe calibration tensions, sample-assignment effects, and the cluster anchor; it cannot be attributed to the intrinsic spatial geometry of the Universe.} The SGLS+QSO data alone leave curvature essentially prior dominated, $Ω_K=0.70^{+6.33}_{-7.12}$, whereas removing only the off-diagonal cluster covariance moves the posterior to $Ω_K=5.21^{+2.46}_{-2.07}$. Thus the cluster anchor supplies most of the curvature constraining power and its covariance materially changes the posterior location.

AI.tldr: 论文重新审视一个结合强引力透镜系统(SGLS)、紫外/X射线类星体(QSOs)与38个SZ/X射线星系团角径距离的晚期、模型无关距离一致性框架，重点研究系统误差而非给出竞争性的曲率测量。

AI.result: 联合后验为Ω_K=2.085^{+1.634}_{-1.103}（68%；95%中心区间[0.269,6.028]）。作者明确指出这一正向偏移由跨探针定标张力、样本指派效应和星系团锚点驱动，不能归因于宇宙内禀空间几何。仅用SGLS+QSO时曲率基本由先验主导，Ω_K=0.70^{+6.33}_{-7.12}；而仅移除星系团协方差的非对角项后，后验移动到Ω_K=5.21^{+2.46}_{-2.07}。

title: Statistical Strong Lensing V. Inference with Microlensed Quasars
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Microlensing of strongly lensed quasars provides direct information on the stellar component of lens galaxies, and can help break the degeneracy between the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and the dark matter. However, a statistical framework to forward model microlensing data while accounting for strong lensing selection effects is still missing. We incorporated microlensing effects into the hierarchical model of Paper III, and investigated to what extent flux measurements of strongly lensed quasars can break the degeneracy between the stellar IMF and the dark matter distribution. We tested the method on a mock sample of 219 doubly imaged quasars, lensed by circularly symmetric lenses. When microlensing effects are modelled, the inference using image fluxes recovers the input foreground population parameters and provides tighter constraints than the inference without flux constraints. The improvement is clearest in the $μ_α-μ_5$ plane, where $μ_α$ describes the mean stellar population synthesis mismatch parameter $\logα_{\rm SPS}$ and $μ_5$ describes the mean projected dark matter mass within $5\,{\rm kpc}$. The 68% credible interval on $μ_α$ shrinks from 0.16 dex to 0.09 dex, with the degeneracy between $μ_α$ and $μ_5$ significantly reduced. By contrast, fitting the image fluxes without accounting for microlensing leads to large biases on the inferred parameters. This work is a first step towards an accurate modelling of microlensing data. Application to real lens samples will require dropping the circular symmetry assumption and adopting more realistic models for the microlensing magnification.

AI.tldr: 本文将微引力透镜效应纳入强透镜化类星体的层级贝叶斯模型，在219个模拟双像系统上验证：建模微引力透镜后，像的通量测量可打破恒星初始质量函数与暗物质之间的退化，μ_α的68%置信区间从0.16 dex缩小到0.09 dex；而忽略微引力透镜直接用通量拟合会产生明显偏差。
AI.motivation: 强透镜化类星体的微引力透镜效应能直接探测透镜星系中的恒星成分，有助于打破恒星初始质量函数（IMF）与暗物质之间的退化。但已有工作（Paper III的层级模型）缺少一个在考虑强透镜选择效应前提下对微引力透镜数据进行正向建模的统计框架。
AI.method: 将微引力透镜效应引入Paper III的层级模型，采用219个由圆对称透镜产生的双像类星体模拟样本进行检验；对比三种推断：带微引力透镜建模并使用像通量约束、不使用通量约束、以及不考虑微引力透镜而直接用通量拟合。参数空间重点关注μ_α（平均恒星族合成失配参数logα_SPS）与μ_5（5 kpc内平均投影暗物质质量）平面。
AI.result: 建模微引力透镜后，利用像通量的推断能恢复输入的前景总体参数，并比不含通量约束的推断给出更紧的限制；在μ_α–μ_5平面上改进最明显，μ_α的68%可信区间由0.16 dex缩小至0.09 dex，且μ_α与μ_5之间的退化显著减弱。相反，不考虑微引力透镜而拟合像通量会导致参数推断出现较大偏差。
AI.conclusion: 本工作是准确建模微引力透镜数据的第一步。应用于真实透镜样本时需放弃圆对称假设，并采用更真实的微引力透镜放大率模型。

title: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via a Halo Model Approach with Space-borne Detectors
comment: 20 pages, 13 figures, 11 tables, to appear in ApJS
summary: Future space-borne gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and DECIGO, are expected to detect a large number of GW events, a fraction of which may be strongly lensed by intervening galaxies or galaxy clusters. In this work, we develop a comprehensive framework to simulate strongly lensed GWs in the context of space-borne detectors. Based on realistic astrophysical models for both the source population and the lens distribution, we construct mock catalogs of lensed GW events, referred to as \textbf{GW-LMC-Space}. Our results show that, for a four-year LISA observation, the expected number of lensed events ranges from $0$ to $131$, depending on the adopted formation model of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs). The corresponding lensing probability for MBHBs can reach up to $\sim 0.3\%$. For DECIGO, we find that the number of lensed events in a one-year observation is expected to lie in the range of $0$--$44$, with a lensing probability of $\sim 0.15\%$ for stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs), binary neutron stars (BNSs), and neutron star--black hole binaries (NSBHs). These results highlight the importance of accounting for signal overlap in the analysis of strongly lensed GW events in future space-borne GW observations.

title: Tracing small-scale structure formation through cosmic time with strong gravitational lensing: A case for a next-generation sub-millimetre/millimetre interferometer
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series
summary: The nature of dark matter and the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in modern astrophysics. Both leave a key signature in an overlapping, largely unexplored mass range: $<10^7$ M$_{\odot}$ dark haloes and wandering black holes. These may be undetectable directly, but detectable through gravitational perturbation of strongly lensed images, and partly or entirely distinguishable from one another through lensing data alone. We demonstrate through realistic simulations that a 255-element sub-mm/mm interferometer could probe this critical mass regime, detecting gravitational perturbations in strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) from objects down to at least $10^5$ M$_{\odot}$. Combined with lens-galaxy characterisation from the European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), which strengthens the physical interpretation of detected perturbers, and the unprecedented lens samples expected from Euclid and the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), this facility could deliver a census of low-mass dark matter haloes and wandering massive black holes across cosmic time.

title: Strong gravitational lensing with Euclid
comment: Contribution to the Focus Point ''Surprises from major new telescopes''
summary: Euclid data is going to lead to the discovery of approximately 10^5 new strong gravitational lenses, thereby increasing the number of known lenses by a factor of 30. Such an impressive jump has the potential to revolutionise the field of strong lensing, by covering an ever-increasing range in the parameter space occupied by the lenses and lensed sources, and by uncovering rare and precious strong lens systems. The first quick data release of Euclid has already revealed hundreds of lenses, giving us a taste of what the final Euclid strong lens sample might look like. These lenses include a variety of objects acting as deflectors, from isolated galaxies to clusters, from early-type galaxies to edge-on disks. As many as four double-source plane lenses, in which one foreground object lenses two galaxies at two different redshifts, have already been discovered. As more data are acquired, it might become possible to detect the strong lensing signature of dwarf galaxy satellites, and to find lenses with an unusually large number of images. In this paper, we try to anticipate the kind of discoveries that these data will bring along.

title: Microcaustics: Fast GPU-Accelerated Dynamical Microlensing of Time-Dependent Extended Sources
comment: 26 pages, 11 figures. Code available at https://github.com/JFagin/microcaustics
summary: Gravitational microlensing probes unresolved quasar accretion disc structure and compact objects in lens galaxies and is an important systematic in strong-lens time-delay cosmography. Most analyses use static microlensing map simulations because evolving individual microlenses and caustics is computationally prohibitive. We present Microcaustics, a GPU-accelerated Python package built on PyTorch for dynamical microlensing of time-dependent extended sources in strong gravitational lenses. It combines a local-exact/far-field deflection solver, source-directed lens-plane scouting with temporal reuse, and biquadratic inverse polygon mapping (IPM). GPU batching and fused Triton rasterization accelerate the calculation, while binary caustic labels track source-centred crossings. Across three simulated quadruply lensed quasar systems, our package generates a 10-year, 147-frame multiband light curve in an amortized median of 0.68 s (0.88 s with labels) on a consumer GPU with a median light-curve RMSE of 0.35 mmag, while recovering every reference source-centred caustic crossing. At comparable map accuracy, the batched throughput is 780 times higher than that of a recent CUDA IPM implementation and extrapolates to a speedup of millions relative to classic GPU-D. We demonstrate that our IPM converges as $N_{\rm ray}^{-0.84}$, approaching the idealized $N_{\rm ray}^{-1}$ convergence rate of piecewise-affine IPM and improving upon the $N_{\rm ray}^{-1/2}$ inverse ray-shooting rate. We also introduce a GPU-resident general relativistic and reverberating quasar source model and demonstrate our method with an evolving supernova source. These advances make fully dynamical stellar fields practical for Bayesian and simulation-based inference.

title: Cosmology with strong gravitational lenses
comment: Reviews of Modern Physics, invited article; 59 pages, 32 figures
summary: Three of the most pressing open questions in cosmology -- the nature of dark energy and dark matter, and the growing tension in the value of the Hubble constant H$_0$ -- call for cosmological probes that are independent of, and complementary to, traditional methods. Strong gravitational lensing offers exactly that: a purely gravitational probe of the universe's expansion history and matter distribution, sensitive to dark matter's presence regardless of whether it interacts with light. Time-delay lenses and multiplane lenses can measure H$_0$ and the dark energy equation of state directly, while the distortion of lensed images can reveal the abundance and internal structure of dark matter subhalos. After a brief theoretical and historical introduction, I review recent breakthroughs enabled by JWST and by advances in lens modeling and stellar dynamics. Examples include the recent measurement of H$_0$ with 3\% precision in flat $Λ$ cold dark matter cosmology, and a tentative detection of dark matter self-interaction. Strong lensing is entering a pivotal era: wide-field surveys with Euclid, Rubin, and Roman, and radio surveys with the Square Kilometer Array, are poised to increase the number of known strong lenses by orders of magnitude, positioning strong lensing to play a central role in answering these open questions in the decade ahead.

title: What fuels the growth of stars and black holes in galaxies through cosmic time? The physics and chemistry of the interstellar medium in distant galaxies
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series. 9 pages 3 figures
summary: The interplay between the baryonic matter in galaxies (gas, dust, stars) has a fundamental role in our understanding of galaxy formation and evolution through cosmic time. The (sub)mm regime provides a unique window to measure the physical conditions and chemistry in the cold and dusty gas reservoirs that fuel the formation of new stars and the growth of massive black holes in distant galaxies. Large sub(mm) interferometers have made a revolutionary impact mapping the cold gas and dust in galaxies beyond the local universe. However, significant progress is hampered by limited spectral-line sensitivity. After more than a decade of surveys, molecular gas (traced by 12CO) has been measured only in a few tens of typical, massive main-sequence star-forming galaxies at z>1, while access to fainter gas-tracing species has been limited to only the very brightest galaxies. Thereby it restricts access to the detailed conditions in the cold gas clouds in typical galaxies in the distant universe. A revolutionary, flagship sub-mm interferometer with a massive increase in instantaneous spectral line sensitivity and broad spectral grasp (ALMA2040) fills this gap by enabling rich, multi-transition, multi-species and multi-isotopologue studies of the atomic and molecular interstellar medium for thousands of typical galaxies across galaxy populations and redshift. This will unveil how the ISM evolves across the galaxy population for statistical samples in different redshift bins, detailed studies of the physical conditions and chemistry in the multi-phase interstellar medium of typical galaxies, and how the cold ISM regulates and responds to star- and black-hole formation, providing a tremendous leap forward in the study of galaxy assembly over cosmic time.

title: Probing ordered magnetic fields in galaxies across cosmic time
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series, 10 pages, 3 figures, additional comments are welcome
summary: Magnetic fields are dynamically important across many astronomical environments, yet their origin, strength, and evolution over cosmic time remain poorly understood. Ordered magnetic fields are ubiquitous in the nearby Universe, as revealed by a range of observational techniques, but evidence for their existence at cosmological distances is scarce. Recent ALMA detections of polarised dust emission indicate that galactic-scale ordered magnetic fields, spanning up to kiloparsec scales, were already present in massive star-forming galaxies at redshifts up to $z\sim5.6$. This white paper argues that the ALMA2040 concept -- with its nearly tenfold improvement in sensitivity and angular resolution, and full-polarisation capability extended to higher-frequency bands -- will open up the study of cosmic magnetism in the early Universe. We identify four science drivers: constraining the dynamos that generate galactic-scale ordered fields, measuring the strength of early magnetic fields, connecting magnetic fields to galaxy evolution across cosmic time, and constraining dust grain properties through the polarised spectral energy distribution. We summarise the corresponding requirements in angular resolution, spectral coverage, and sensitivity, and discuss synergies with next-generation telescopes.

The dust continuum observation at 0.3 arcsec resolution is shown as contours. b) : The central part of the right subimage of 9io9 (marked by the yellow square), where the polarisation signal and lens amplification are both strong. c) : The best-fit model of the magnetic fields in the source plane, adopted from de Roo et al. title: ALMA2040: The High-Redshift Circumgalactic Medium. Imaging the fueling and feedback of galaxies in the early universe
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series. 11 pages, 2 figures
summary: Galaxies do not form in isolation, but rather as part of a wider interconnected web mediated at their interface by an extended gaseous atmosphere - the Circum-Galactic Medium (CGM). This dynamic and multiphase region is fed and shaped by gas inflows and mergers from the intergalactic medium and by feedback-driven outflows and radiation from the central galaxy. The CGM is imprinted by the past, present and future evolution of its central galaxy and environment. The cool atomic and molecular phases are of particular interest as they dominate the mass budget of outflows and provide a reservoir of direct star forming fuel for the galaxy to accrete. In the early universe where accretion rates, mergers, and feedback processes peak, the cycle of gas through the CGM is most vigorous. Sub-mm observations have detected cold gas in extended halos and gas flows around high redshift galaxies but are thus far limited to the most massive, extreme or gravitationally lensed sources, using just a handful of the strongest emission and absorption lines. A significant increase ($5-10\times$) in spectral line sensitivity compared with the current ALMA is needed to push physical scales, densities and properties to a new regime. We present three key scientific cases for an ALMA2040 telescope: (i) direct imaging of extended [CII]-traced CGM halos around Milky-Way-progenitor galaxies at $z=4$-8; (ii) resolved detection of cold, clumpy outflows on $\sim$100 pc scales tied to individual star-forming clumps; and (iii) multi-species/-transition emission and absorption diagnostics that jointly constrain the density, chemistry, and radiation fields permeating the cool CGM and its multiphase gas flows.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 星系并非孤立形成，而是作为更广泛互联网络的一部分，其界面由延展的气体大气——环星系介质（CGM）所介导。这一动态且多相的区域受到来自星系际介质的气体流入和并合以及中心星系的反馈驱动外流和辐射的供给与塑造。CGM 被其中心星系和环境的过去、现在和未来演化所印记。冷的原子和分子相尤其令人关注，因为它们主导了外流的质量预算，并为星系吸积提供了直接恒星形成燃料的储库。在早期宇宙中，吸积率、并合和反馈过程达到峰值，气体通过 CGM 的循环最为剧烈。亚毫米波观测已在高红移星系周围的延展晕和气体流中探测到冷气体，但迄今为止仅限于最大质量、极端或引力透镜源，且仅使用少数最强的发射线和吸收线。与当前 ALMA 相比，光谱线灵敏度需要显著提高（$5-10\times$），才能将物理尺度、密度和性质推向新 regime。我们提出 ALMA2040 望远镜的三个关键科学案例：(i) 直接成像 $z=4$-8 的银河系祖星系周围由 [CII] 示踪的延展 CGM 晕；(ii) 解析探测与单个恒星形成团块相关的 $\sim$100 pc 尺度冷、团块状外流；(iii) 多物种/多跃迁发射和吸收诊断，联合约束渗透冷 CGM 及其多相气体流的密度、化学和辐射场。

figures.caption_en: Figure 1 : Deep ALMA view of the lensed galaxy A1689-zD1 ( \(z=7.13\) , \(\mu\simeq 9.3\) ; 7.8 hr on-source in Band 6; Watson et al. 2015 ; Knudsen et al. 2025 ). (a) JWST/NIRCam colour image with [C ii ] 158 \(\mu\) m contours (2–64 \(\sigma\) ): the cool gas extends far beyond the stellar body. The inset shows the [C ii ] velocity field. (b) Real part of the [C ii ] visibilities versus \(uv\) distance. A two-component compact plus extended model is required to fit the [C II ] data while the dust (grey) stays compact, the direct interferometric signature of a cool-gas halo ( Akins et al. 2022 ) .
figures.caption_zh: 图 1：透镜星系 A1689-zD1（\(z=7.13\)，\(\mu\simeq 9.3\)；Band 6 源上 7.8 小时；Watson et al. 2015；Knudsen et al. 2025）的深度 ALMA 视图。(a) JWST/NIRCam 彩色图像及 [C ii ] 158 \(\mu\) m 等值线（2–64 \(\sigma\)）：冷气体远远延伸到恒星体之外。插图显示了 [C ii ] 速度场。(b) [C ii ] 可见度实部与 \(uv\) 距离的关系。需要双组分紧凑加延展模型来拟合 [C II ] 数据，而尘埃（灰色）保持紧凑，这是冷气体晕的直接干涉特征（Akins et al. 2022）。

figures.caption_en: Figure 2 : High line sensitivity and resolution are required to detect and resolve cold outflows at \(z\sim 5\) , illustrated here in the galaxy CRISTAL-02 from the CRISTAL Large Program ( Davies et al. 2026 ; Herrera-Camus et al. 2025 ) . JWST imaging and IFU spectroscopy resolve the galaxy into 5 star-forming clumps, ‘a–e’ (upper left). Only Clump ‘b’ shows signs of an outflow in cold ([C II ] 158 \(\mu{m}\) ) or warm gas (H \(\alpha\) ; upper right), and the cold gas phase dominates the total outflow mass (lower panel), similar to archetypal local-universe winds. ALMA2040 will reach \(\approx\) 30 \(\times\) lower-mass galaxies that are far more numerous than this case study. Reproduced from Davies et al. (2026) .
